test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT the correct statement about escape velocity?

options.text: In our solar system, Jupiter has the highest escape velocity.
On the earth, escape velocity is 11.2 km/s.
Escape velocity depends on the mass and radius of the celestial body.
In our solar system, Venus has the lowest escape velocity.

solution:
The correct answer is **option 4 **as **Mercury has the lowest escape velocity **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The** escape velocity ****of Jupiter** is the **highest** in the solar system with** 59.5 km/s. Thus, statement 1 is correct**
 
• The escape velocity of Earth is **11.19 (11.2) km/s. Thus, statement 2 is correct**
 
• Escape velocity depends on the** mass and radius of the celestial body**. **Thus, statement 3 is correct**
 
• The escape velocity of **Mercury is the lowest with 4.25 km/s** whereas **Venus has an escape velocity of 10.36 km/s**. **Thus, statement 4 is NOT correct**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **The minimal speed at which a free, unpropelled item must move in order to escape a main body's gravitational pull is known as escape velocity or escape speed.**
 
• The speed at which an item's** total kinetic energy** plus its** gravitational potential energy** equals zero is known as escape velocity.
 
• The formula for escape velocity is

 V=2gR" id="MathJax-Element-30-Frame" role="presentation" style=" position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=2gR−−−−√ V=2gR V=2gR" id="MathJax-Element-30-Frame" role="presentation" style=" position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=2gR−−−−√ V=2gR V = sqrt 2gRV=2gR" id="MathJax-Element-30-Frame" role="presentation" style=" position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=2gR−−−−√ V=2gR 

where **g is the acceleration due to gravity** and **R is the radius of the planet**

 
• This expression results from **energy conservation** and is** independent of the direction in which the body is thrown or projected.**
 
• The angle of projection has **no effect on escape velocity.**
 
• So, the escape velocity remains the same at **11 km/sec.**
